differences.title: 1. RENDERING STRATEGY
differences.leftDesc: Enhanced server rendering capabilities, leveraging React Server Components for optimal performance and reduced client load.
differences.rightDesc: Primarily client-side rendering, with server-side rendering as an option, suitable for simpler applications.

differences.title: 2. LAYOUTS
differences.leftDesc: Supports powerful nested layouts, enabling consistent UI structure across different routes with shared components.
differences.rightDesc: Layouts are managed per page, offering less flexibility for shared UI elements.

differences.title: 3. DATA FETCHING
differences.leftDesc: Fetch data directly within Server Components, simplifying data fetching logic and improving security.
differences.rightDesc: Relies on specific data fetching functions (`getStaticProps`, `getServerSideProps`) at the file level.

differences.title: 4. ROUTING MECHANISM
differences.leftDesc: Routes are defined by folders, offering a more intuitive and organized way to structure complex applications.
differences.rightDesc: Routes are defined by file names within the `pages` directory, which can become unwieldy.

differences.title: 5. LOADING STATES
differences.leftDesc: Leverages React Suspense for elegant loading states, providing a seamless user experience.
differences.rightDesc: Requires manual implementation of loading states, often using conditional rendering.

differences.title: 6. API ROUTES
differences.leftDesc: API endpoints are created using dedicated `route.js` files within route segments, integrating seamlessly.
differences.rightDesc: API endpoints reside in a top-level `pages/api` directory, separate from page structure.

differences.title: 7. PERFORMANCE OPTIMIZATION
differences.leftDesc: Optimized for minimal JavaScript on the client by default, utilizing Server Components for efficiency.
differences.rightDesc: Relies on SSR/SSG for initial load, but can result in more client-side JS for interactivity.
